reports.verdict: Moderna swung to a profit on 29% revenue growth and raised its sales outlook, but much of its higher cash comes from new debt.

takeaways.label: Revenue outlook raised
takeaways.text: Third-quarter revenue rose 29% to $1.3B, driven by international COVID vaccine deliveries. Full-year growth is now seen at 15–25%, up from 'up to 10%'.

takeaways.label: Cash jump is mostly debt
takeaways.text: Year-end cash is now seen at $8.1–8.3B versus $4.7–5.2B before. This reflects $2.6B net from convertible notes, not just better operations.

takeaways.label: Melanoma shot is the real prize
takeaways.text: Phase 3 data with Merck showed the cancer vaccine cut recurrence or death risk by 42%. Regulatory filings are being prepared.

takeaways.label: Flu launch limited, norovirus stalled
takeaways.text: The flu vaccine was approved in August but launches only in a limited way this season. The norovirus vaccine's path forward is unclear, with no added cohort this season.

reports.verdict: DraftKings slashed 2026 profit guidance to fund a $650-700 million bet on prediction markets, promising a bigger 2027 revenue rise.

takeaways.label: Profit outlook slashed
takeaways.text: Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA (a profit measure) is now $175-275 million, down from $700-900 million. Revenue guidance also fell, to $6.35-6.55 billion from $6.5-6.9 billion.

takeaways.label: Predictions spending ramps up
takeaways.text: DraftKings now plans $650-700 million of Predictions investment in 2026, with revenue from it immaterial. Without it, the core business would earn $875-925 million.

takeaways.label: 2027 growth promise
takeaways.text: First 2027 outlook: revenue $7.35-7.75 billion, about 17% growth at the midpoint, with profit of $800 million-$1 billion after about $300 million of Predictions spending.

takeaways.label: Growth, but bigger losses
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 16% to $1.33 billion and paying users 13% to 4.1 million. Marketing jumped to $606 million, and the quarterly loss widened to $469 million.

reports.verdict: Growth sped up to 39% and Cloudflare guided far above expectations, but gross margin keeps slipping and GAAP profit has not arrived yet.

takeaways.label: Big guidance jump
takeaways.text: Q4 revenue is guided to $845–846M versus about $798M expected. Full-year revenue is guided to $2.963B, up from $2.864–2.870B in August.

takeaways.label: GAAP profit pulled forward
takeaways.text: The CFO said GAAP profitability should arrive in Q4 2026, versus an earlier end-2028 target. Q3 still showed a $67.9M operating loss.

takeaways.label: Margin slippage
takeaways.text: Gross margin fell to 72.4% (non-GAAP) from 75.3% a year ago. Management pointed to the lower-margin Workers developer platform and said it still improves operating margins.

takeaways.label: AI demand broadening
takeaways.text: Pay-per-crawl, which charges AI firms for site access, produced its first revenue, with OpenAI paying. An AI company also signed an $11M Workers deal.

reports.verdict: Record sales came from Alani Nu, but costs keep squeezing margins, the flagship CELSIUS brand is still shrinking, and fourth-quarter growth will slow.

takeaways.label: Margins keep sliding
takeaways.text: Gross margin fell to 46.8% from 51.3% a year ago and 48.1% last quarter. Aluminum and diesel costs rose further, and management expects only high-40s for the full year.

takeaways.label: Alani Nu carries growth
takeaways.text: Alani Nu sales rose 24% to $410M, with a record seasonal flavor. CELSIUS brand sales fell 6% to $357M, and management said it is 'not yet where we want it to be.'

takeaways.label: Growth slows next
takeaways.text: Fourth-quarter growth is guided below the first three quarters. About $20-25M of shipments were pulled into Q3, and last year's quarter had a one-time inventory benefit. No numeric targets were given.

takeaways.label: Reorganization and fixes
takeaways.text: Brand-led leadership is now in place, with new presidents for CELSIUS and Rockstar. Management says 2027 'will look very different' for CELSIUS, with new flavors and a second North Carolina production line.

reports.verdict: Opendoor quadrupled its home buying into a collapsing housing market, so margins are shrinking, losses are widening, and its profit goal is slipping.

takeaways.label: Margins shrinking further
takeaways.text: Contribution margin fell to 3.3% from 5.8% last quarter. Management expects it to fall again in Q4, with adjusted EBITDA loss guided to $70M–$85M versus $31M in Q3.

takeaways.label: Housing market weakened
takeaways.text: The CEO said home sales 'started to collapse' in Q3 with mortgage rates above 7%. Opendoor chose to cut prices and clear homes rather than protect margin.

takeaways.label: Balance sheet getting heavier
takeaways.text: Inventory hit $2.57B (7,596 homes) versus $1.05B a year ago. Homes listed over 120 days doubled to 18% from 9% last quarter. $2.0B of asset-backed debt is now due within a year.

takeaways.label: Profit goal behind schedule
takeaways.text: Management admits it is behind its aim of positive adjusted net income by end-2026, even as it guides Q4 revenue up at least 40% on 4,865 homes bought.

reports.verdict: PENN's casinos beat expectations and its online business guided to a first profitable quarter, but a $20 million full-year Interactive loss still stands.

takeaways.label: Online losses nearly gone
takeaways.text: Interactive lost $18.3 million versus $76.6 million a year ago. Management guides to an $18.7 million profit in Q4, a $20 million full-year loss, and profit in 2027.

takeaways.label: Casinos beat, outlook raised
takeaways.text: Casino revenue hit $1.5 billion with profit margin up for a third straight quarter. Full-year casino profit guidance rose $10 million to $1.973 billion.

takeaways.label: Debt falling, buybacks eyed
takeaways.text: Net debt fell to $1.8 billion from $2.2 billion at year-end. Management says share buybacks are 'front of mind' for 2027, after paying down debt.

takeaways.label: Alberta launch gaining fast
takeaways.text: Online sports betting in Alberta is nearing its Ontario market share after three months. The launch cost $20 million, which explains why 2026 Interactive is no longer breakeven.

reports.verdict: Margins hit a five-year high, but sales keep shrinking and Q4 revenue is guided lower, to $54-59 million.

takeaways.label: Q4 outlook falls
takeaways.text: Q4 revenue is guided to $54-59 million, below Q3's $64.5 million (down 8.1% from a year earlier). The company cites 'ongoing uncertainty and volatility' and gives no profit guidance.

takeaways.label: Margins improve, sales don't
takeaways.text: Gross margin hit 19.3% versus 7.4% a year ago, the highest in five years, from cheaper production. Volume still fell 10.9%, and the CFO said low volume muted the gains.

takeaways.label: U.S. keeps shrinking
takeaways.text: U.S. retail fell 13.2% on a 20.8% volume drop, mainly lost club-store distribution. Europe-led international retail grew 13.3%, but international foodservice fell 19.4%.

takeaways.label: Cash burn slows, debt stays
takeaways.text: Nine-month operating cash use fell to $37.3 million from $101.2 million. Cash is $169.3 million against $313.9 million of debt, and $14.5 million of notes come due March 2027.

reports.verdict: Snap's profits surged on cost discipline, but 4% ad growth and shrinking North American users keep the growth story unproven.

takeaways.label: Profit jumped
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA (core profit) hit $383M versus $182M a year earlier, and net income was $56M versus a loss. Costs barely rose while revenue grew 14% to $1.72B.

takeaways.label: Ad growth is weak
takeaways.text: Ad revenue grew only 4%, which Spiegel called below ambitions. Brand advertising fell on weaker packaged-goods spending, while performance-focused ads grew.

takeaways.label: North America users falling
takeaways.text: North American daily users fell 6% to 92M, and total daily users of 495M missed expectations. From 2027 Snap will report monthly users instead, with no regional breakdown.

takeaways.label: Q4 outlook
takeaways.text: Snap guided Q4 revenue to $1.95B-$1.985B and adjusted EBITDA to $490M-$525M. The revenue midpoint is slightly above the roughly $1.95B analysts expected.

reports.verdict: CVS raised 2026 profit guidance again and lifted its 2027 floor to $8.65, as Aetna's Medicare repair drives the recovery.

takeaways.label: Aetna margin recovery
takeaways.text: Health insurance profit jumped to $912M from $314M a year ago. The share of premiums spent on care fell to 91.3% from 92.8%, mainly on Medicare.

takeaways.label: Higher 2026 outlook
takeaways.text: 2026 adjusted earnings guidance rose to at least $8.20 per share from $7.90–$8.10. Expected operating cash flow rose to at least $15.5 billion from $11.5 billion.

takeaways.label: 2027 floor raised
takeaways.text: Management now expects at least $8.65 per share in 2027, up from about $8.44. The pharmacy-benefit unit is seen at a trough of at least $7B profit.

takeaways.label: Company split planned
takeaways.text: Management is pursuing a separation of the company. Analysts pressed on the costs, and management called them manageable and already in guidance without giving numbers.

reports.verdict: Uber beat its own bookings and profit guidance, with 20% growth intact, while shifting its focus to rolling out driverless cars.

takeaways.label: Beat own guidance
takeaways.text: Gross bookings rose 20% to $59.8B, above the ~$59.25B guidance midpoint. Adjusted EPS of $0.88 hit the top of guidance. Trailing free cash flow hit a record $10.4B.

takeaways.label: Steady Q4 outlook
takeaways.text: Q4 bookings guidance is $63.25–65.25B (18–22% growth), and adjusted EPS is $0.95–0.99. Management called growth 'steady' rather than accelerating.

takeaways.label: Driverless cars go commercial
takeaways.text: Uber expects about 700 fully driverless vehicles by year-end and 2,000+ by end of 2027, citing a 30% utilization edge. It wants outside capital to fund the fleets.

takeaways.label: Overseas driver shortage
takeaways.text: Driver supply lagged rider demand in several international markets, including Brazil, India and Canada. The CFO blamed higher fuel costs from the Middle East war. Management said October supply hours accelerated.

reports.verdict: Profit is still falling about 15%; the higher full-year earnings forecast comes from a lower tax rate, not from better operations.

takeaways.label: Raise is tax-driven
takeaways.text: Full-year earnings forecast rose to $2.07-$2.13 a share from $2.03-$2.09, which management attributed mainly to a lower tax rate. Operating profit is still guided down 16-18%.

takeaways.label: US still shrinking
takeaways.text: North America sales fell 3.2% on lower volumes, pulling total organic sales down 1.1%. Emerging Markets grew 15.6%. The sales outlook's low end improved to down 1.25%, despite a roughly 1-point hit from SNAP cuts.

takeaways.label: 2027 looks costly
takeaways.text: Management expects inflation slightly above 5% in 2027, brand spending to stay near this year's $700 million extra level, and price increases to be 'likely' needed.

takeaways.label: Share losses easing
takeaways.text: The portion of sales gaining or holding market share rose to 28% from roughly 25% in the first half. The CEO said share has 'leveled out', but recovery is not yet visible.

reports.verdict: MetLife posted its highest-ever quarterly adjusted profit per share, but much of the jump came from volatile investment gains rather than core growth.

takeaways.label: Record profit
takeaways.text: Adjusted earnings per share excluding one-time items rose 22% to $2.85, MetLife's best quarter ever. Adjusted return on equity reached 19.6%.

takeaways.label: Investment gains boost
takeaways.text: Variable investment income, which swings with markets, jumped 49% to $720 million and was a main driver of the profit increase, so it may not repeat.

takeaways.label: Growth in every segment
takeaways.text: Premiums and fees excluding large pension deals grew 8% to $13.5 billion, rising in all six segments. Europe, the Middle East and Africa led at 17% constant-currency growth, up from a year ago.

takeaways.label: Mixed spots
takeaways.text: Retirement and Income Solutions earnings fell 6% after an annual assumptions review. Latin America profit excluding one-time items fell 5% in constant currency on lower investment returns. Asia sales fell 6%.

reports.verdict: Kodak's chemicals business is growing 21% while print shrinks 7%, leaving profit up only slightly and print earnings nearly gone.

takeaways.label: Chemicals carry the quarter
takeaways.text: Advanced Materials & Chemicals revenue rose 21% to $99 million, and its operating profit (EBITDA) rose to $21 million from $16 million. It is now Kodak's most profitable unit.

takeaways.label: Print is weakening
takeaways.text: Print revenue fell 7% to $165 million, and its operating profit (EBITDA) dropped to $1 million from $8 million. That is a sharp slide from the $8 million profit it earned last quarter.

takeaways.label: Profit growth is modest
takeaways.text: Operating profit (EBITDA) rose just $2 million to $31 million, below last quarter's $36 million. Net income of $21 million was helped by interest expense falling to $3 million from $18 million.

takeaways.label: Cash rebuilt
takeaways.text: Cash rose $27 million to $317 million after falling last quarter. Year-to-date cash from operations is break-even, and inventories are up $44 million for the year.

reports.verdict: Shopify held 32% growth and a record 22% cash margin, but the first revenue miss in four years and a flat fourth-quarter outlook cooled enthusiasm.

takeaways.label: First revenue miss
takeaways.text: Revenue of $3.74B (up 32%) came in just under analyst estimates of about $3.75B, reportedly the first miss in about four years. Sales volume rose 29% to $119B, also slightly light.

takeaways.label: Cash margin flattered
takeaways.text: The 22% free cash flow margin included temporary boosts: a marketing test, tax timing and an accounting change. The Q4 guide is merely flat with last year's Q4, and Q4 spending steps up.

takeaways.label: Steady holiday outlook
takeaways.text: Q4 revenue growth is guided to the low thirties, matching Q3. Gross profit is guided to grow in the high twenties, and operating costs to run 29–30% of revenue.

takeaways.label: AI shopping still small
takeaways.text: Orders from AI-driven traffic rose 3.3x, but management called volume small. Shopify also paid about $100M for Shop.com and is spending more on AI tools.

reports.verdict: Teva beat profit forecasts and raised its brand-drug outlook, but the Austedo boom faces a Medicare pricing hit from January.

takeaways.label: Brand drugs driving growth
takeaways.text: Austedo, Ajovy and Uzedy together grew 33% to about $1.1 billion. 2026 Austedo guidance rose to $2.55–2.65 billion and total revenue guidance to $16.7–17.0 billion.

takeaways.label: Austedo pricing headwind
takeaways.text: Management expects Austedo sales to fall year over year in Q4 and flagged Medicare price changes in January. The CEO still sees peak sales above $3 billion.

takeaways.label: Profit beat, sales slipped
takeaways.text: Adjusted EPS was $0.86 versus $0.78 a year ago, and margins widened. Revenue still fell 2% to $4.4 billion because generic Revlimid sales dropped.

takeaways.label: Stronger balance sheet
takeaways.text: Teva refinanced about $4.7 billion of notes, and Moody's and S&P upgraded it to investment grade. Total debt is still $16.7 billion.

reports.verdict: Pfizer raised 2026 guidance on strong Eliquis and new-drug sales, but flat quarterly revenue shows COVID and vaccine declines still weigh.

takeaways.label: Guidance raised
takeaways.text: Full-year revenue outlook rose $1.5B at the midpoint to $62-64B, and EPS to $2.95-$3.05 from $2.80-$3.00, driven by Eliquis and newer drugs.

takeaways.label: Eliquis and new drugs
takeaways.text: Eliquis grew 25% on lower rebates and higher demand. Launched and acquired products rose 32%, and non-COVID sales rose 7%. Padcev jumped 55%.

takeaways.label: COVID and vaccines drag
takeaways.text: Revenue was flat at $16.6B. Paxlovid fell 63%, Comirnaty 29% and Prevnar 10% on lower vaccination rates and shrinking adult share.

takeaways.label: Obesity and patent cliff
takeaways.text: Pfizer targets a first approval for its monthly obesity drug in 2028. It also added $2.5B of 2027-2029 cost cuts to cushion coming patent expiries.

reports.verdict: AMD's AI data center business nearly doubled and the fourth-quarter forecast is far above Wall Street's, though margins and cash flow lag the growth.

takeaways.label: Data center surge
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 45% to $13.4B, above AMD's own guidance. Data center sales jumped 97% to $8.5B, now about 64% of the total.

takeaways.label: Big Q4 guide
takeaways.text: AMD guided fourth-quarter revenue to about $17B, against analyst estimates near $16.2B. Management says growth accelerates as Helios AI racks and Venice server chips ramp.

takeaways.label: 2027 ambition
takeaways.text: Lisa Su now expects revenue to grow more than 80% in 2027, a sharp step up in the long-term growth story.

takeaways.label: Margins and cash lag
takeaways.text: Gross margin is guided to about 55%, down from 56%. Free cash flow fell to $554M from $1.5B a year ago. Gaming sales dropped 40%.

reports.verdict: Refining profits hit another record on war-inflated margins, and management expects them to stay high through mid-2027 while it sells two refineries for cash.

takeaways.label: Record margins again
takeaways.text: Profit per barrel refined jumped to $45.70 from $17.60 a year ago. Adjusted earnings were $26.93 a share, above the roughly $24.5 analysts expected.

takeaways.label: Margins seen lasting
takeaways.text: Management expects elevated margins through at least mid-2027, citing about 10 million barrels a day of global refining capacity offline, and says it has seen no demand destruction.

takeaways.label: Selling two refineries
takeaways.text: Marathon is selling its St. Paul Park and Mandan refineries to CVR Energy for $4.2 billion, with $3.45 billion going to Marathon. Proceeds go mainly to the Gulf Coast.

takeaways.label: Heavy cash return
takeaways.text: Marathon returned $3.3 billion in the quarter, raised its dividend 10% and added a $5 billion buyback authorization. It holds $13.6 billion in cash.

reports.verdict: Record quarter, but Apple guided December gross margin down to 45%–46% as memory costs climb, and gave no outlook past that.

takeaways.label: Margins squeezed by memory
takeaways.text: December-quarter gross margin is guided to 45%–46%, below the 47.9% just reported (about 1 point of which came from tariff refunds) and below the 46.3% analysts expected. Memory prices are still rising.

takeaways.label: Growth slowing
takeaways.text: December-quarter revenue is guided up 7%–10%, down from 12% this quarter. Services is guided up 8%–9%. Mac and iPad supply stays limited by memory availability.

takeaways.label: AI spending climbing
takeaways.text: Operating expenses are expected to rise 11%–13% next quarter on AI investment. R&D already jumped about 32% to $11.7 billion in the September quarter.

takeaways.label: Strong quarter and year
takeaways.text: Revenue was $114.5 billion (up 12%) and EPS $2.10, both September-quarter records. iPhone grew 17% to $57.6 billion and Greater China grew 21%. Full-year revenue hit $479 billion.

reports.verdict: Palantir's revenue nearly doubled again and U.S. commercial sales passed government for the first time, but new contract signings are growing far slower than sales.

takeaways.label: Commercial overtakes government
takeaways.text: U.S. commercial revenue rose 148% to $984M, passing U.S. government revenue ($953M, up 96%) for the first time. Total revenue topped $2B, up 96% to $2.31B.

takeaways.label: Guidance raised sharply
takeaways.text: Full-year revenue outlook rose to about $8.53B, roughly 91% growth, from $8.15B. Q4 is guided to about $2.65B, with adjusted operating margin near 62%.

takeaways.label: Bookings lag revenue
takeaways.text: New U.S. commercial contract value grew only 11% to $1.46B, and total contract value grew 6%. Management said several large deals had shorter terms than usual.

takeaways.label: Land-and-expand accelerating
takeaways.text: Pilots are turning into much larger deals, for example $3M to $29M annual value. Customers who stay spend 65% more each year (net retention 165%).
